title: The One-Dimensional Wave Equation
short: The wave equation in one dimension
lead: A pulse sent down a rope keeps its shape as it travels, and a plucked string vibrates in place between its fixed ends. Both are waves in one dimension, described by the sine wave and the classical wave equation.
objectives: To introduce the wave equation including time and position dependence
summary_html: Waves which exhibit movement and are propagated through time and space. The two basic types of waves are traveling and stationary. Both exhibit wavelike properties and structure (presence of crests and troughs) which can be mathematically described by a wavefunction or amplitude function. Both wave types display movement (up and down displacement), but in different ways.Traveling waves have crests and troughs which are constantly moving from one point to another as they travel over a length or distance. In this way, energy is transmitted along the length of a traveling wave. In contrast, standing waves have nodes at fixed positions; this means that the wave’s crests and troughs are also located at fixed intervals. Therefore, standing waves only experience vibrational movement (up and down displacement) on these set intervals - no movement or energy travels along the length of a standing wave.
notes: Adapted from Michael Fowler (University of Virginia); Figures 2.1.2 and 2.1.3 are folded into one moving figure, as are Figures 2.1.4 and 2.1.5.

exercises.source_id: The simplest wave is the (spatially) one-dimensional sine wave
exercises.prompt: A wave on a rope is $A(x,t) = (0.020\ \text{m})\sin(4.0\pi x - 10\pi t)$, with $x$ in meters and $t$ in seconds. Find (a) its maximum amplitude, (b) its wavelength, (c) its frequency and (d) the speed at which it travels.

parts.hint: The phase kx grows by 2π over one wavelength.
The phase ωt grows by 2π over one period.

answer.solution: Compare with $A(x,t) = A_o\sin(kx - \omega t + \phi)$: $A_o = 0.020$ m, $k = 4.0\pi$ rad/m and $\omega = 10\pi$ rad/s. (a) $A_o = 0.020$ m. (b) The wave repeats when $kx$ grows by $2\pi$, so $\lambda = 2\pi/k = 2\pi/4.0\pi = 0.50$ m. (c) At a fixed $x$ it repeats when $\omega t$ grows by $2\pi$, so $\nu = \omega/2\pi = 5.0$ Hz. (d) A crest keeps $kx - \omega t$ fixed, so it moves at $v = \omega/k = 10\pi/4.0\pi = 2.5$ m/s.

exercises.source_id: is called the classical wave equation in one dimension
exercises.prompt: Show that any traveling wave $y(x,t) = f(x - vt)$ of Equation 2.1.1, whatever the shape $f$, satisfies the classical wave equation, Equation 2.1.2.

answer.hint: Write $s = x - vt$ and use the chain rule for each derivative.
answer.solution: Let $s = x - vt$, so $\partial s/\partial x = 1$ and $\partial s/\partial t = -v$. By the chain rule $\partial y/\partial x = f'(s)$ and $\partial^2 y/\partial x^2 = f''(s)$, while $\partial y/\partial t = -v f'(s)$ and $\partial^2 y/\partial t^2 = v^2 f''(s)$. Then $\dfrac{1}{v^2}\dfrac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = f''(s) = \dfrac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}$, which is Equation 2.1.2 for any twice-differentiable $f$.
